items.stem: Why does Wang Han stop writing after writing the first word?
options: He doesn't know the first word.
He thinks the sentence has a mistake.
He wants to ask Ms Chen a question.
He is too nervous to write.
items.quote: “That’s not right. But is it OK to point out the mistake? Is that polite, in the first lesson?” Questions jump into my mind.

items.stem: According to Wang Han, who is the sentence from?
items.quote: “Ms Chen, there’s a mistake,” I say. “That sentence is from Confucius, not from Mencius.”

items.stem: What is Ms Chen’s main lesson for the students?
items.quote: to think more in your learning. Please always remember this.

items.stem: In the letter, junior high is compared to what?
items.quote: But junior high is like a river.

items.stem: What do Mia's parents tell her to do when she has to sail her boat by herself?
options: Try her best and work hard
items.quote: Just try your best and work hard.

items.stem: Who wrote the letter to Mia?
items.quote: Yes, and it’s also a letter from Mum and me.

items.stem: What is the father's love like according to the writer?
items.quote: His love may be silent. But like a mountain, it is always there.

items.stem: What does the father do when he is happy about his son's growth?
options: He hides his care in his heart
items.quote: But he just hides his care in his heart.

items.stem: When the son carries his father across the river, what happens to the father?
items.quote: Tears quietly run down his face.

items.stem: What is Robert's problem in the story?
items.quote: But Robert has a serious disease and cannot move at all.

items.stem: How does John help Robert for the first time?
options: He puts him in a trailer and pulls it with his bike.
He buys him a new bike.
He carries him on his back.
He asks other kids to play with him.
items.quote: He puts Robert in a trailer and pulls it along with his bike.

items.stem: What is the main message of the passage?
options: Love is powerful and always wins.
items.quote: And love always wins.

items.stem: What does Leng never regret?
options: Having little time with her family
items.quote: But she never regrets her decision to be an ER doctor.

items.stem: Why do medical workers in China give up their family time?
options: To answer the call of duty
items.quote: They give up their family time to answer the call of duty.

items.stem: In the passage, what shines brighter than fireworks?
items.quote: In the heart of every patient, their hard work shines brighter than fireworks.

items.stem: Where does Worker No. 55 work?
items.quote: He works in Workshop 1001 in the Leaf.

items.stem: What do workers in the Leaf collect during the day?
items.quote: They collect sunlight and CO2 during the day.

items.stem: According to the passage, why is oxygen important to animals and humans?
options: They use it to make sugar.
items.quote: It means a lot to animals and humans, though – they need it to breathe!

items.stem: According to the passage, which drink is the most popular in the world after water?
items.quote: What is the most popular drink in the world after water? The answer is tea.

items.stem: For the writer from Chengdu, what does a cup of warm tea make them feel?
items.quote: A cup of warm tea always makes me feel like I’m back home.

items.stem: According to the British writer, what is tea for their family?
items.quote: We chat and relax in the yard with black tea and biscuits. It’s our way of connecting.

items.stem: What did Henry think of pigeons when he first watched them in the park?
items.quote: Pigeons are BORING and DIRTY!

items.stem: What surprising fact did Henry learn from his online research?
options: Pigeons can recognise themselves in mirrors
Pigeons can fly at speeds of over 100 km per hour
There are over 200 kinds of pigeons
Pigeons can fly several thousand kilometres without getting lost
items.quote: Pigeons can recognise themselves in mirrors.

items.stem: How did Henry describe pigeons at the end of the passage?
items.quote: Well, pigeons aren’t boring or scary. They are AMAZING – I just didn’t know enough about them!

items.stem: Where can you see dodos now?
items.quote: But now you can only see us in museums.

items.stem: Why did dodos die out?
options: Because humans hunted them and their animals ate their eggs
Because they had no food to eat
Because there were too many dodos
items.quote: They cut down the trees and our lovely forest was gone. They hunted us because we were slow and couldn’t fly. What’s more, their pigs, cats and dogs ate our eggs.

items.stem: What does the author ask people to do?
items.quote: help them. Make them as happy as a clam, not as dead as a dodo.
